items.title: [whyred/sdm660] Modem crash loop with err_qdi / ipa_bam when initializing mobile data (4GB RAM variant memory constraints & uC SMMU limitation)
items.body:
[dmesg_log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29990309/dmesg_log.txt)

### Device Information
* **Device**: Xiaomi Redmi Note 5 Pro (whyred)
* **SoC**: Snapdragon 636 / 660
* **RAM/Storage Variation**: 4GB RAM / 64GB Storage
* **OS / Kernel**: postmarketOS, Mainline Linux v7.0.9 (sdm660-mainline tree)
* **Modem Driver**: `ipa2-lite`
* 
### Description
We successfully compiled and integrated the `ipa2-lite` driver into the mainline v7.0.9 kernel for the Xiaomi Redmi Note 5 Pro (whyred). While the modem is successfully recognized by ModemManager and registers onto the network (e.g., SMS, USSD, and GSM calls are functional), we encountered two distinct critical crashes when attempting to initialize packet data services (Mobile Data).

#### Issue 1: Initial Boot/Allocation Crash Loop (Mitigated via disabling ZRAM)
On the 4GB RAM variant, the default postmarketOS initialization of a large ZRAM (5.3 GB) and Swapfile fragments the 32-bit DMA/CMA contiguous memory space. As the Hexagon DSP (MSS) boots up, the host driver fails to cleanly reset the IPA pipes, throwing the following assertion on the modem firmware side:

com-q6v5-mss 4080000.remoteproc: fatal error received: ipa_bam.c:732:IPA Assert: ipa_bam_hw_pipe_get_sw_ofst_reg(pipe_num) == 0 failed
remoteproc remoteproc0: crash detected in 4080000.remoteproc: type fatal error


* **Mitigation**: Disabling ZRAM completely (`deviceinfo_zram_swap_pct="0"`) resolves this boot loop, allowing the modem to register stably.

#### Issue 2: Hard Crash on Toggling Mobile Data Connection (uC SMMU Probing Constraint)
When attempting to activate the Mobile Data connection (either via `nmcli` or `nmtui` simple connect), the modem Hexagon DSP crashes immediately, bringing down both the cellular radio and the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth subsystem (WCN3990 ath10k) due to shared SSR lines. 

The kernel logs capture the following crash signature:

qcom-q6v5-mss 4080000.remoteproc: fatal error received: err_qdi.c:459:EX:wlan_process:1:WLAN RT:1083:PC=b00c87e0
remoteproc remoteproc0: crash detected in 4080000.remoteproc: type fatal error
ath10k_snoc 18800000.wifi: firmware crashed!



---

### Root Cause Analysis
This behavior aligns with the known limitation of the current `ipa-lite` driver port on SDM660/636/630 SoC series. Currently, the driver does not support probing/mapping the microcontroller SMMU (`uc-smmu`). 

When packet services are initiated, the modem microcontroller (uC) attempts to access memory registers through a wrapper that fails to resolve page addresses due to the missing SMMU mappings. This results in an AXI bus fault leading to the `wlan_process` crash on the Hexagon DSP.

---

### Log Snippets
Here is the sequence of the connection crash:
1. `NetworkManager` triggers data activation.
2. Modem attempts interface setup.
3. DSP registers `err_qdi.c` / `wlan_process` failure.
4. Host times out awaiting handshake:
   `ipa 14780000.ipa: error -110 awaiting init driver response`
5. Subsystem Restart loop starts.

---

### Proposed Goal / Request
We are requesting guidance or assistance from the community in implementing `uc-smmu` probing/bypass support in the mainline `ipa2-lite` driver for the SDM660/636 family. Any patches or legacy references from downstream kernels that cleanly handle the uC IOMMU mapping constraints for Qualcomm MSM8996/8953 (which share similar IPA architecture) would be highly appreciated.

items.title: qcom: add initial mainline support for OPPO R11/T (CPH1707)
items.body:
This pull request adds initial mainline Linux support for the OPPO R11, based on the Qualcomm SDM660 platform.

The device tree and supporting drivers now provide the core hardware enablement required for regular device use, including:

* Correct volume-key definitions and RMI4 capacitive navigation keys
* Correct touchscreen orientation
* Wi-Fi MAC address provisioning through the WLFW QMI interface
* Initial Qualcomm ASoC audio support
* BQ27541 fuel-gauge support
* Status LED and camera flash LED support
* USB host-mode VBUS control
* Battery charging with device-specific current and voltage limits

The charging configuration initially uses conservative settings and restores the validated R11 charging limits once the required power-supply support is available.

With these changes, the OPPO R11 can boot with its major onboard peripherals described and managed by the mainline-style kernel stack.

items.title: Add support for the Vsmart Active 1 (zangyapro)
items.body:
Adds the **Vsmart Active 1** (PQ6001) -- a rebrand of the BQ Aquaris X2 Pro (LineageOS codename `zangyapro`, https://wiki.lineageos.org/devices/zangyapro/), very close to jasmine, so the dts is derived from `sdm660-xiaomi-jasmine`.

Working: eMMC (HS400), USB, UART, WCN3990 Bluetooth, Adreno 512 (zap shader), PMIC (charger / fuel gauge / keys), and the DSI display.

For the display I extended the mainline `panel-himax-hx83112a` driver (was Fairphone 3 only, 1080x2340) into a multi-variant driver and added the **DJN 1080x2160** variant. This is a TDDI panel whose full register init is done by the bootloader -- the downstream vendor kernel DT also ships only exit-sleep + display-on for this panel and its HX83112A siblings (DJN/Truly/DJN11), so the variant only sends those two commands and leaves reset deasserted. Needs `CONFIG_DRM_PANEL_HIMAX_HX83112A`.

The microSD slot (`&sdhc_2`) is enabled using the supplies and card-detect GPIO taken from the downstream device tree. I do not have a microSD card on hand, so it is **not runtime-tested** -- happy to drop it if you would prefer.

Tested on hardware (6.19.10): panel lights through the real DPU+DSI+panel pipeline (`card0-DSI-1` connected, 1080x2160), GPU freedreno FD512, WiFi/BT/SSH all work.

The in-cell touchscreen is not wired up yet.



---
Rebased onto the current `qcom-sdm660-7.0.y` branch per review; supersedes #185.

items.title: ath10k: snoc: fix unbalanced IRQ enable in crash recovery
items.body:
From: `Caleb Connolly <caleb.connolly@linaro.org>`

In `ath10k_snoc_hif_stop()` we skip disabling the IRQs in the crash recovery flow, but we still unconditionally call enable again in `ath10k_snoc_hif_start()`.

We can't check the `ATH10K_FLAG_CRASH_FLUSH` bit since it is cleared before `hif_start()` is called, so instead check the `ATH10K_SNOC_FLAG_RECOVERY` flag and skip enabling the IRQs during crash recovery.

This fixes unbalanced IRQ enable splats that happen after recovering from a crash.

Fixes: 0e622f67e041 `("ath10k: add support for WCN3990 firmware crash recovery")`
